title: 1969 AHSME Problem 31
statement: Let \(OABC\) be a unit square in the \(xy\)-plane with \(O(0,0),\) \(A(1,0),\) \(B(1,1),\) and \(C(0,1).\) Let \(u=x^2-y^2\) and \(v=2xy\) define a transformation of the \(xy\)-plane into the \(uv\)-plane. The transform (or image) of the square is:

solutions.text:
The vertices map as \[ \begin{aligned} O&\mapsto(0,0),\\ A&\mapsto(1,0),\\ B&\mapsto(0,2),\\ C&\mapsto(-1,0). \end{aligned} \] Side \(OA\) maps to the segment from \((0,0)\) to \((1,0),\) and \(CO\) maps to the segment from \((-1,0)\) to \((0,0).\) On \(AB,\) \(x=1,\) so \(u=1-\frac{v^2}{4};\) on \(BC,\) \(y=1,\) so \(u=\frac{v^2}{4}-1.\) These are the two upper parabolic arcs joining \((\pm1,0)\) to \((0,2).\)

Therefore, the correct answer is D.
hints: Map the four vertices and then transform each side separately
The horizontal sides and vertical sides become two line segments and two parabolic arcs
